Previous slide Next slide Frequently Asked Questions How long will my new roof last? The life expectancy of a new roof varies based on the size, weather, and roofing material. Asphalt shingle roofing materials last anywhere from 20-30 years, while metal roofing can last 50-100 years. We’ll discuss the longevity of all types when we give you an estimate. What should I do with a roofing emergency in Sanpete County? While we don’t currently offer emergency services, we encourage you to contact us immediately after an emergency. The faster we can get there, the more we can minimize the damage. What are the signs that my roof needs repair or replacement? If you notice dark spots on your ceiling or water inside your home, you may need a new roof. Other signs of roof damage include missing or broken shingles, higher utility bills, and sunlight coming through the roof. Get Estimate How Can You Tell If You Need New Windows Aren’t sure if you need new windows? Watch for some of the following problems that are clear signs you need to give us a call to discuss your options. High Utility Bills: When your windows don’t latch right or are too old, they let inside air out, making it hard to manage the internal temperature and putting extra pressure on your heating and cooling system. Drab-Looking Windows: Your windows have a life expectancy, just like every other material in your home, and once they start looking old and drab, it might be a good idea to replace them. Difficulty Opening or Closing: If you have to work hard to open or close your windows, you may have a warped frame or loose hinges and springs, signs that you need new windows. If you’ve been getting by with roof repair but think it might be time to have yours replaced, consider the following signs it’s time to invest in replacement. Sagging Roof: A sagging roof is a sign that water is accumulating in a spot on your roof and that the material is weakening. Missing Shingles: One or two damaged or missing shingles can be repaired, but once they start to come off more often, it’s time to replace the roof.
